title: Impact of Close-Election Incumbency on Reelection Probability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) is the appropriate method here. The incumbency advantage can be identified by exploiting the discontinuous jump in treatment probability at the vote-share threshold (running_var = 0). The key assumption is that candidates just above and below the cutoff are comparable in all other characteristics except for winning the election, allowing us to isolate the causal effect of incumbency on reelection probability.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s88_data.csv")

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0)

# Print main results
cat("=== REGRESSION DISCONTINUITY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect (Incumbency Advantage):", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(rdd_result$se[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_result$pv[1], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(rdd_result$ci[1,1], 4), ",", round(rdd_result$ci[1,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("Bandwidth:", round(rdd_result$bws[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Observations:", rdd_result$N_h[1] + rdd_result$N_h[2], "\n\n")

# Robustness check 1: Different bandwidth
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 0.5)
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: Half Bandwidth ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_half_bw$pv[1], 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness check 2: Double bandwidth
rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0, h = rdd_result$bws[1] * 2)
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: Double Bandwidth ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_double_bw$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_double_bw$pv[1], 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness check 3: Different polynomial order
rdd_p2 <- rdrobust(y = data$y, x = data$running_var, c = 0, p = 2)
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 3: Quadratic Polynomial ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_p2$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(rdd_p2$pv[1], 4), "\n\n")

# Check for manipulation (McCrary test)
rdd_density <- rddensity(data$running_var, c = 0)
cat("=== MANIPULATION TEST ===\n")
cat("McCrary Test P-value:", round(rdd_density$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")
if(rdd_density$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("No evidence of manipulation (p > 0.05)\n\n")
} else {
  cat("Potential manipulation detected (p < 0.05)\n\n")
}

# Visual inspection
cat("=== SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Main RDD Estimate:", round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("Interpretation: Winning a close election changes reelection probability by", 
    round(rdd_result$coef[1], 4), "percentage points\n")

# Create visualization
plot_data <- data[abs(data$running_var) <= rdd_result$bws[1] * 1.5, ]
rdplot(y = plot_data$y, x = plot_data$running_var, c = 0, 
       title = "RDD Plot: Incumbency Advantage", 
       x.label = "Vote Share Margin", 
       y.label = "Reelection Probability")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive incumbency advantage of approximately 0.05-0.15 (5-15 percentage points). This is based on the extensive political economy literature showing that incumbent politicians benefit from advantages such as name recognition, access to resources, ability to deliver targeted benefits to constituents, and media attention. The effect should be statistically significant, as the incumbency advantage is one of the most robust findings in political science. The magnitude reflects the substantial but not overwhelming advantage that comes with holding office in a competitive electoral environment.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze the discontinuity at the vote-share cutoff to isolate the effect of incumbency.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Winning a close election reduces the probability of reelection.
